name: Newton's shell theorem (potential constant, field zero, at every point inside a uniform spherical shell)

source.located: I. Newton, Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica (1687), Book I, Propositions 70 (a body inside a uniform spherical shell under an inverse-square attraction feels no net force) and 71 (outside, as if the mass were at the centre). No arXiv copy; the Principia itself is NAMED-NOT-READ. READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT in two arXiv papers: (a) A.R. Klotz, 'The Gravity Tunnel in a Non-Uniform Earth', arXiv:1308.1342v1 (2013), p.2 eq.(1): 'the force of gravity F_G acting on a test mass m at radial position r comes from the mass of the sphere below the object, due to the shell theorem: F_G(r) = -Gm(4/3 pi rho r^3)/r^2'; (b) J. de Haro, 'Novikov Coordinates and the Physical Description of Gravitational Collapse', arXiv:2601.18660v1 (2026), p.10: 'by virtue of the shell theorem [29], the motion of a dust particle located inside the star satisfies r'' = -GM(r)/r^2, where M(r) denotes the mass enclosed within the sphere of radius r', with [29] = Newton, Principia (1687), UC Press translation (1999). Both restate the theorem in its enclosed-mass form, of which the tree's interior-null form is the special case 'no mass enclosed'; NEITHER prints Prop. 70 verbatim, so the exact piecewise statement (-M/R inside, -M/d outside) is DERIVED here from the inverse-square kernel by an exact sympy integral (rederive S1) rather than quoted. GR analogue used as a cross-check: Birkhoff's theorem, READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT in N.V. Johansen and F. Ravndal, arXiv:physics/0508163v2 (2005) p.1: Birkhoff (1923; Jebsen 1921) 'showed that the static Schwarzschild metric (1) is a solution outside any mass distribution, even when this varies with time as long as the spherical symmetry is maintained'.

published_statement: Principia I Prop. 70 (as restated, and as re-derived here): if a particle is placed inside a spherical shell whose surface density is uniform, and it is attracted to every point of the shell by a force inversely proportional to the square of the distance, it is attracted by no net force, at every interior point. Prop. 71: outside, the shell attracts as if its whole mass were at its centre. Restated forms read: Klotz 1308.1342 eq.(1) (the field at r comes only from the mass below r 'due to the shell theorem'); de Haro 2601.18660 p.10 (r'' = -GM(r)/r^2, M(r) the enclosed mass, 'by virtue of the shell theorem [29]'). In potential form (derived, S1): Phi_shell(d) = -GM/R for d < R (constant), -GM/d for d > R.
published_hypotheses: H1 the attraction between elements is exactly inverse-square in distance (Newtonian gravity; also true for the Hooke r-law, not for general kernels)
H2 the shell is exactly spherical with uniform surface density (or a union of such concentric shells; spherical symmetry of the SOURCE)
H3 the attracted body is inside the shell cavity (for Prop. 70) -- a point, or any body wholly contained in the cavity (superposition)
H4 static Newtonian statics: the force is the instantaneous sum of pairwise attractions (superposition/linearity of the source); no finite-propagation or relativistic correction
H5 (implicit in Newton's era, not a stated hypothesis) positive masses only; negative mass is not contemplated
hypothesis_drift: ADDED, VERIFIED -- negative mass (H5 widened): stability.py:74-77 and 106-108 ('whatever the signs', negmass.py:67-70) apply the theorem to a NEGATIVE core. Valid: the shell's interior field is zero independent of the test body, and the force m_core*g = 0 for either sign; direct quadrature at d/R = 0, .25, .5, .9, .99 gives |F| < 1e-16 for m_c = +1 and -1 (rederive S5), and the third-law force on the rigid shell is likewise zero. Not a drift in the theorem's content.

ADDED, VERIFIED -- carried into the linearised metric: concentric.py:57-60 puts the constant interior potential into g_tt and claims 'NOTHING to the tidal field'. sympy (S4): the metric diag(-(1+2c),(1-2c),(1-2c),(1-2c)) with c constant has Riemann identically zero (exactly, not only to first order), and for any Phi the linearised R^x_{txt} = d_x^2 Phi, so a constant interior Phi contributes a pure clock-rate (delay) term and zero tidal field. The shell delay/core advance budget concentric.py:325 = (L/R_s)/(2 ln(L/a)) evaluates to 0.0780 at L=300, R_s=200, a=0.02, matching the verdict's '~8 %' (concentric.py:360-362).

SCOPE (not a dropped hypothesis of the theorem) -- concentric.py:358-359 VERDICT 'The shell delays without focusing, by Newton's shell theorem' is printed unqualified; the theorem gives it only for rays wholly inside r < R_s (H3). The owner states that condition at concentric.py:30-31 ('a ray at b << R_s passes wholly inside') and the measured ray (X0=-150, LAM=300, b=1; concentric.py:156-160) reaches r_max = 150.003 < R_s = 200, so every number the file prints is inside the theorem's class. A ray that CROSSES the shell meets Ricci (matter) focusing 8 pi sigma / cos(alpha) per crossing (jump of dPhi/dr = m/R_s^2 = 4 pi sigma, S3); two crossings against the core's focal power 4m/b^2 give b^2/R_s^2 = 2.5e-5 at b=1 (S7). Non-zero, negligible at the design point, and outside what the file measures.

SCOPE -- stability.py:74-77 / 269-272 'the core feels no force wherever it sits inside ... NEUTRAL, EXACTLY' needs the core wholly inside the cavity (H3). Exact for stability.py's own model (a point interior mass M_in, Schwarzschild interior, stability.py:128-160). For the concentric.py device core, a Plummer sphere m/sqrt(r^2+a^2) (concentric.py:164-168), which is not compactly supported, 1.5e-8 of the core mass (= 1.5 a^2/R_s^2) lies beyond R_s = 200 at a = 0.02, and a displaced core then feels F_z = +7.11e-14 (d=50) and +2.22e-13 (d=100) for m = 1, m_c = -1 -- 2.8e-9 and 8.9e-9 of M m/R_s^2, directed outward (S8, cross-checked by 40-digit mpmath). 'Exactly' holds for a compact core; for the Plummer core it holds to O(a^2/R_s^2). Recorded as a discrepancy of wording, not a refutation.

NAMED BY THE OWNER, NOT DROPPED -- rigid shell (H2 maintained under the core's pull): the displaced core's field is non-uniform over the shell, so a deformable shell would lose uniform density and the interior null; stability.py:88-90 names this as NOT-RUN item 2. The theorem is used only on the rigid-uniform class, which the owner states.

NAMED BY THE OWNER, NOT DROPPED -- Newtonian gravity (H1, H4): stability.py:111-112 and 123 mark the GR junction-condition version NOT-RUN; concentric.py:139-141 names the linearised weak field (Phi_max ~ 0.25) as the weakest point. For the CONCENTRIC (spherically symmetric) configuration the shell-contributes-no-interior-tidal-field part survives in full GR by Birkhoff's theorem applied to the vacuum region inside the shell (restated in physics/0508163 p.1; the interior corollary is not printed in the read text and is inferred here); for a DISPLACED core no GR statement is read or checked here.

HYPOTHESIS PROBE -- exact inverse-square (H1) is load-bearing: with a Yukawa-corrected kernel (1 + alpha e^{-r/lambda})/r the interior potential becomes -alpha M lambda e^{-R/lambda} sinh(d/lambda)/(R d) (sympy, S9), no longer constant; at alpha = 0.01, lambda = R, d = R/2 the interior field is dPhi/dd = -6.3e-4 M/R^2, and alpha -> 0 recovers the theorem. The tree's hypothesis 'Newtonian / linearised GR' includes exact inverse-square, so this is not a drift, but it is the hypothesis on which 'zero force at every interior point' rests.

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS, exit 0 (32 checks). S1/S2: exact angular integral of the inverse-square kernel over a uniform shell gives Phi = -M/R inside (independent of d) and -M/d outside; interior gradient and all nine interior Hessian (tidal) components identically zero. S3: the tree's encoding -m/max(r,R_s) is exactly that piecewise form; jump in dPhi/dr at R_s = m/R_s^2 = 4 pi sigma. S4: metric with constant Phi has Riemann == 0 exactly; linearised R^x_{txt} = d_x^2 Phi. S5: direct quadrature force on an off-centre point core, d/R = 0 to 0.99, both signs: |F| <= 8.3e-17 (quadrature validated outside: F(2R) = -0.250000000000); third-law force on the rigid shell zero. S6: shell delay / core advance = 0.0780 at the design point, matching the verdict's '~8 %'; the measured ray stays inside (r_max = 150.003 < 200). S7: a crossing ray's shell (Ricci) focusing relative to the core's = b^2/R_s^2 = 2.5e-5. S8: Plummer core tail beyond R_s = 1.5e-8 of its mass; displaced-core force 7.11e-14 (d=50), 2.22e-13 (d=100), outward, agreed to 8 digits by an independent 40-digit mpmath quadrature. S9: Yukawa-corrected kernel gives a non-constant interior potential -alpha M lambda e^{-R/lambda} sinh(d/lambda)/(R d); alpha -> 0 recovers the theorem.

lacked_data: What Newton (1687) lacked that the tree relies on, taken one at a time. (1) GENERAL RELATIVITY: the tree carries the interior constant potential into g_tt. Having GR does not change the conclusion: S4 shows a constant-Phi metric is exactly flat (Riemann == 0, not only to first order), and for the spherically symmetric configuration Birkhoff's theorem (read via physics/0508163) makes the region inside a shell independent of the shell except for a clock rescaling. For a DISPLACED core in GR nothing is read or computed here; the tree itself marks that NOT-RUN (stability.py:111-112, 123). (2) NEGATIVE MASS: never contemplated in 1687. Having it does not change the conclusion: the theorem is a statement about the shell's field, and m_core*0 = 0 for either sign (S5, both signs to 1e-16). (3) PRECISION TESTS OF THE INVERSE-SQUARE LAW: Newton inferred the exponent from planetary data. The theorem is exactly as strong as that law: S9 shows any Yukawa admixture breaks the interior null in closed form. Modern laboratory tests exist and are named (refs in 2609.09485) but were not read, so no bound is quoted; within the tree's stated framework (Newtonian limit of GR) the exponent is exactly 2 and nothing moves. Evidence either way: no datum found or computed here moves the conclusion as the tree uses it; the only places the theorem's reach is narrower than an unqualified sentence in the tree are geometric scope (crossing rays, a non-compact core), quantified at 2.5e-5 and <1e-8, not missing data.
grade_evidence: The statement the tree uses -- inside a uniform spherical shell the potential is constant, the field vanishes at every interior point (not only the centre), and the shell contributes nothing to the interior tidal field, whatever the sign of the body inside -- is re-derived exactly (sympy S1-S3: Phi_in = -M/R, zero gradient, zero Hessian) and confirmed by direct quadrature at five off-centre positions for both core signs (S5, |F| < 1e-16, validated by the exterior -M m/d^2 to 12 digits). Its passage into the linearised metric is checked symbolically (S4). The tree's hypotheses (exactly spherical uniform thin shell encoded as -m/max(r,R_s); Newtonian/linearised gravity; rigid shell, with shell response flagged NOT-RUN) match the source's H1-H4; the negative-mass widening is verified, not assumed. The owner's own numerical consequence (shell delay ~8 % of core advance) is reproduced (0.0780). Two scope discrepancies are recorded, not graded as narrowing: the unqualified verdict 'the shell delays without focusing' (concentric.py:358-359) is exact for rays wholly inside -- which is every ray the file measures (r_max = 150.003 < 200) and the condition it states at lines 30-31 -- and off by b^2/R_s^2 = 2.5e-5 for a crossing ray; 'neutral, EXACTLY' (stability.py:73-77) is exact for a compact core and holds to 1.5 a^2/R_s^2 ~ 1e-8 for the non-compact Plummer core of concentric.py. No moved datum bears on the theorem inside the tree's stated framework. Source caveat: the Principia is NAMED-NOT-READ; the theorem is read via two arXiv restatements (enclosed-mass form) and its exact interior form is established here by derivation, and alphaXiv was over quota so later-literature search did not run.
what_would_change_the_grade: To NARROWED: if the tree (or a later file) uses the shell theorem for rays that cross the shell or for a core not wholly inside the cavity at a level where b^2/R_s^2 or a^2/R_s^2 is not negligible -- e.g. a design with R_s comparable to b or a -- or quotes 'no force' for a deformable shell or a displaced core in full GR (not read or computed here; the owner marks it NOT-RUN). To DATA-DEPENDENT: if the tree's physical scale (the core mass m fixing R_s = 200 m) placed the device in a range where the inverse-square law is not experimentally established, and a read bound on a Yukawa alpha(lambda) there were large enough that S9's interior field competed with the effects the tree measures. To WRONG: only a demonstrated non-zero interior field for an exactly uniform shell under an exact inverse-square law, which S1 excludes analytically. Reading the Principia Prop. 70 text itself would upgrade the source status, not the grade.
